nodes.label: Fast First Kill Principle
nodes.rationale: First kill should happen within 60 seconds. Enemies are passive/slow with low HP. Satisfying feedback: screen shake, sound, damage numbers. This teaches core loop (Fight → Get Reward → Progress) immediately.

nodes.label: Soft Start (No Forced Tutorial)
nodes.rationale: All top Roblox sword RPGs use a soft start with no forced tutorial. Roblox players have extremely low tolerance for tutorial walls and will leave instantly. Player is immediately in control with quest-based learning via 'Kill 5 Bandits' which teaches combat, quest loop, navigation, and rewards simultaneously.

nodes.label: PvP Balance Framework
nodes.rationale: Balance levers: cooldown timers, global cooldown, end-lag, posture/guard break, level brackets, stat normalization. Hybrid rock-paper-scissors + linear power model. Deepwoken is ~80% skill-based; Blox Fruits is ~30% skill / 70% stats. Arena should normalize stats; open world can use partial normalization.

nodes.label: Additive Awakening Model (Dominant Pattern)
nodes.rationale: Overwhelming trend: DON'T RESET. Stack new layers (Race V2, V3, V4, Fruit Awakening, Fighting Style mastery) on top without losing progress. Modern Roblox players (Gen Alpha/young Gen Z) have very low tolerance for forced progress reset. Each tier should be 5-15 hours, with visual rewards and 3-6 sub-milestones.

nodes.label: Ideal Sword RPG Design Pillars
nodes.rationale: Players want: skill-based combat (Deepwoken depth) with clear onboarding, massive open world (Blox Fruits scale), build diversity, fair cosmetic-only monetization, respectful progression, robust endgame with procedural dungeons and guild wars, both PvE and PvP equally supported, active developer communication

nodes.label: Sword RPG Fair Monetization Pledge (10 rules)
nodes.norm_label: sword rpg fair monetization pledge (10 rules)
nodes.rationale: No exclusive power; time vs money (paying speeds up, never gates); transparent odds; no predatory FOMO (items return on rotation); respect young players (no dark patterns); free alternatives for every dev product; trading economy; PvP balance (cosmetic-only premium); clear value with exact quantities/probabilities; generous codes

nodes.label: Monetization Best Practices
nodes.rationale: Sell convenience not power; create first-purchase pipeline; use tiered pricing with volume discounts; offer limited-time bundles; allow trading of purchased items; make private servers available; never sell exclusive combat-advantage items; never use gacha for core progression; price entry-level passes below 500 Robux

nodes.label: Progression Dead Zone (Where Players Quit)
nodes.rationale: Players quit at sea transitions (Sea 1→2 at level 700, Sea 2→3 at 1500) because new grind starts with harder enemies. Mid-game islands with slow quest XP also cause churn. Mitigate with guided introduction and power spikes at each transition.

nodes.label: Anti-Patterns (What Never to Do)
nodes.rationale: Never make strongest content pay-only; PvP advantages should come from skill not time investment; permanent loss is polarizing; regular content cadence is more important than large infrequent updates; always communicate balance changes with reasoning and provide compensation paths

nodes.label: Environmental Rhythm Pattern (3-zone cycle)
nodes.rationale: Follow a 3-zone cycle to prevent visual fatigue: Zone A = grounded/natural biome (forest, desert, snow), Zone B = built environment (village, fortress, prison), Zone C = fantastical/breakout zone (sky island, underwater, volcano). Every 4th zone should feel like a milestone with dramatic environmental shift.
